title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 88
paragraphs: Having suffered this outrage from the Aeginetans, the Athenians no longer held back from contriving every possible injury against them. There was in Aegina a man of note named Nicodromus son of Cnoethus. He had a grievance against the Aeginetans, who had previously driven him out of the island, and when he heard that the Athenians were now resolved to do harm to Aegina, he came to an agreement with them to hand the island over to them, telling them on what day he would make his attempt and by what day they must be ready to come to his support.
